latin.665: §. X. Quarta Autoris Probatio urserat, dignam corporis Christi in Cœna S. discretionem, tanquam fidei Christianæ essentialem, necessario verò doctrinam de S. Cœna intemeratam, supponentem, qualis non esset Negatio Oralis Manducationis.
latin.666: Huic retundendæ cùm monuissem, non quemvis errorem de S. Cœna, e. g. errorem circa Indignorum Manducationem, dignam corporis Christi discretionem impedire, dummodo intemerata maneat Spiritualis Manducatio, quæ etiam, extra Sacramentum Cœnæ, dari posset, & actu daretur.
latin.667: Cariss. Wittebergensis, duo regerit §. XVIII. (1) Errorem de Manducatione Indignorum, levem non esse (2) Circa ipsam Corp. & Sang. Christi præsentiam, & Sacramen. Manducationem, a Reformatis errorem committi, utcunque etiam pallietur, certissimum esse.
latin.668: Cui respondeo ad prius: De gravitate ac levitate erroris, quod ad Indignorum Manducationem attinet, dispiciemus Annotat. proximè sequenti.
latin.669: Ad posterius: Autorem in aprico ponere, disputationem suam pro Oralis Manducationis Fundamentalitate, ullius roboris fieri aliter haud posse, quin suffulciatur protrito satis commentô de negata à Reformatis corporis Christi in S. Cœna, præsentia, etiam ab ipso Beza, Disputatori nostro hic loci allegato, prorsus explosô rejectóque, quando Sacram Domini Cœnam evacuari scribit, si minus quis per fidem, præsentissimam esse Christi Carnem, in Cœna fateatur.
latin.670: Nisi fortè qui hoc fatetur, Cœnam S. evacuèt; aut non possit Christi corpus per fidem præsens esse, cùm tamen totus Christus per fidem in cordibus nostris habitet; aut præsentia corporis per fidem, sit merè imaginaria & inane commentum (uti calamus Autoris mentem fortè ejus præcurrens, tantum non blasphemat) perque consequens, fides mera Imaginatio & inane Commentum sit; aut denique, qui per fidem, carnem Christi præsentissimam statuit, hic ipse neget, corpus Christi, ceu objectum fidei, in Cœna, etiam jam ante fidem exsertam, in eadem præsens esse, atque prout præsens est, fidei offerri ac exhiberi. Vid. Tractat. meum Germ. §. XV. pag. 64.

pass_a.665: §. X. The Author’s Fourth Proof had pressed that worthy discernment of Christ’s body in the Holy Supper, as essential to Christian faith, necessarily presupposes untainted doctrine of the Holy Supper — which Negation of Oral Eating would not be.
pass_a.666: When, to blunt this, I had warned that not every error about the Holy Supper — e.g. error about the Eating of the Unworthy — impedes worthy discernment of Christ’s body, so long as Spiritual Eating remains untainted, which could also be given, and actually is given, even outside the Sacrament of the Supper.
pass_a.667: The dearest Wittenberger rejoins two things in §. XVIII. (1) That the error about Eating of the Unworthy is not light. (2) That about the very presence of Body & Blood of Christ, and Sacramental Eating, error is most certainly committed by the Reformed, however it may be palliated.
pass_a.668: To which I reply to the first: Concerning the gravity and lightness of the error, as it pertains to Eating of the Unworthy, we shall examine in the Annotatio next following.
pass_a.669: To the latter: The Author sets in the open that his dispute for the Fundamental character of Oral Eating can otherwise gain no strength unless propped by the sufficiently worn fiction of presence of Christ’s body in the Holy Supper denied by the Reformed — a fiction utterly exploded and rejected even by Beza himself, cited here by our Disputant, when he writes that the Lord’s Sacred Supper is emptied if one does not confess Christ’s Flesh most present in the Supper by faith.
pass_a.670: Unless perhaps he who confesses this empties the Holy Supper; or Christ’s body cannot be present by faith, though the whole Christ dwells in our hearts by faith; or presence of the body by faith is mere imagination and empty fiction (as the Author’s pen, perhaps outrunning his mind, all but blasphemes) and consequently faith itself is mere Imagination and empty Fiction; or finally he who by faith sets Christ’s flesh most present himself denies that Christ’s body, as object of faith, is present in the Supper even before faith is exerted, and as present is offered and exhibited to faith. See my German Tractate §. XV. p. 64.

665: §.X opens the Author’s Fourth Proof: worthy discernment of Christ’s body in the Supper is treated as essential to Christian faith.
That claim, he urged, necessarily assumes an untainted Supper doctrine — which denying Oral Eating would not leave intact.
666: Strimesius had already answered: not every Supper error blocks that discernment — for example, error about the unworthy eating.
So long as Spiritual Eating stays sound, discernment can stand; and Spiritual Eating can be given, and is given, even outside the Supper sacrament.
667: The Wittenberg friend (§.XVIII) replies with two counters: first, the Indignorum error is not a light one.
Second, he says it is certain the Reformed err on the presence of body and blood and on sacramental eating — however they soften the charge.
668: Reply to the first: how heavy or light the Indignorum error is belongs in the Annotatio that follows next.
This locus therefore does not settle that gravity question here.
669: Reply to the second: the Author himself shows his Oral-fundamentality case has no force unless propped by the worn fiction that the Reformed deny Christ’s bodily presence in the Supper.
Even Beza — whom the Disputant cites here — exploded that fiction, writing that the Lord’s Supper is emptied if one will not confess Christ’s Flesh most present in the Supper by faith.
670: Unless confessing presence by faith empties the Supper; or Christ’s body cannot be present by faith though the whole Christ dwells in our hearts by faith; or faith-presence is empty imagination (the Author’s pen nearly blaspheming) so that faith itself becomes empty fiction.

Or unless he who sets Christ’s flesh most present by faith denies the body is already present in the Supper as faith’s object before faith is exerted, and as present is offered to faith — see German Tractate §.XV p.64. Stop §.X before §.XI.
